archetype: Five-colour legendary-permanent toolbox: a repeatable battlefield tutor funded by a multi-colour mana engine, defended by a legendary tax shell, and closed by the Najeela combat loop verified in stack 002. strategic_frame.json declares exactly that; deck-audit establishes no archetype ('none - base targets apply'), so every target below is the base template and the 39 creature copies are read against nothing.
verdict: This deck deploys its commander on schedule and then cannot afford her. Sisay lands at a median turn 3 and 99.1% by turn 6, the mana base is 55 sources against a target of 39 with zero unconditional taplands, and the deck still averages 4.894 available mana on turn 5 against an ability that costs five coloured pips with no generic in it. What limits it is that {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} bill — the same cost Najeela's loop re-charges every combat — and no axis measures it. The colour-sources reading of -15 is not that problem: black carries only 7 pip-bearing cards, so mana_analysis's 20% quorum is 2 cards and the deck holds exactly 2 double-black costs — cutting either one takes the axis to -1.

gaps: Nothing in the repo measures whether five DISTINCT coloured pips are simultaneously available. mana_analysis reports on-curve probability per colour and goldfish reports mean available mana; the deck's central cost is the joint event, and neither artifact answers it. A goldfish extension or a bespoke hypergeometric would settle it.

data/decks/sisay/deck_recon.json does not exist (deck-audit freshness.recon.present = false), so there is no inclusion-rate evidence for this commander. Every add above comes from the deck's own considering.json, which is a candidate list, not a meta signal.

manabase.land_colors models no static mana grant, so Chromatic Lantern and Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth cannot move colour-sources however much mana they actually fix — recomputed, Lantern moves it -15 to -14 and Urborg over a Plains moves it not at all while lowering white. The axis is the wrong instrument for them and neither is prescribed here on that basis.
bracket_report.json for this deck carries no `target` or `within_target` key, so 'is this deck inside its intended bracket' is unanswered by the artifact; the floor of 4 is all that is known.

deck-audit established no archetype for this deck, so the creature, curve and tutor axes are read against base targets. The strategic frame declares a toolbox archetype; the audit's archetype detector does not see it.

manabase.effective_pips sizes a colour against the heaviest requirement that 20% of that colour's pip-bearing cards share, so a colour with few pip-bearers is sized off a very small set: black's 7 cards put the quorum at 2, and the deck's 2 double-black costs are exactly that quorum. The instrument is behaving as designed, but '-15 sources short' overstates how much of the deck the shortfall serves. A per-colour sensitivity report — which single cards move a source target, and by how much — would settle it.

card_roles.json files Sheoldred, the Apocalypse as draw:engine and her oracle draws no cards — she is a draw payoff. So the card-advantage count of 7 holds at least one card that draws nothing while missing four that do, and the number is a floor in one direction and a ceiling in the other without saying so. A role-vs-oracle audit of draw:* across the fleet would settle how common that is.

findings.note: My open finding is closed, and closed by removal rather than hedging. Recomputed the swap with the real code (mana_analysis.nonland_producer_kind + manabase.land_colors/pip_requirements/source_targets over expand_copies(cards.json)): before W26/U22/B21/R21/G27, after (+Rite / -Kodama) W27/U23/B22/R22/G28 — every one of the twelve evidence leaves is exact, the axis moves -15 -> -14, and R lands at 22 of 22 ('red level'). Rite alone gives the identical totals, because nonland_producer_kind(Kodama) is None (land_colors returns {G} but the kind gate rejects it), so the cut contributes nothing to sources — the doc attributes the whole +1 to Rite, correctly. mean_bodies_by_turn['6'] = 4.066 verbatim from goldfish_metrics. The framing is not a softer version of the old claim: the old sentence asserted the card does not move the axis, the new one states that it does, states by how much, and then makes a SEPARATE argument — that manabase models no static grant, so one source is not what the card does — which is the same blindness gaps[2] already records for Chromatic Lantern ('Lands you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color"' vs Rite's 'Creatures you control have...'; both are counted as exactly one five-colour source). Card is {1}{G}, identity G, legal_commander legal. Residual I checked and am not opening: 'with Sisay that is five separate taps' idealises away summoning sickness on {T} mana abilities; the figure is a turn-6 mean over bodies mostly deployed on earlier turns, and the doctor demonstrably knows the rule — add_candidates[3] routes Intruder Alarm's untap through dorks ALREADY on the battlefield rather than through the entering creature.

The pricing now rests on real costs. Sheoldred's oracle is quoted verbatim ('Deathtouch / Whenever you draw a card, you gain 2 life. / Whenever an opponent draws a card, they lose 2 life' — exact modulo newline-to-slash) and the 7 -> 6 is correctly labelled a taxonomy movement, not lost draw. The costs that now lead are real and independently verified: Sheoldred is a Legendary Creature at mana value 4 and Sisay's ability reads 'a legendary permanent card with mana value less than Sisay's power', so power 5 is right; Kambal, Consul of Allocation drains on 'Whenever an opponent casts a noncreature spell', a genuinely different trigger; threat-density is 3 in the audit. Recomputed the mana counterfactual: cutting Sheoldred ALONE takes B's effective_pips 2 -> 1, target 36 -> 22, worst colour -15 -> -1 and B's achieved probability 0.610 -> 0.895 — bit-identical to cutting Dauthi alone, so 'the mana maths does not choose between them' is exact. cost_of_cutting is distinct from why (why = the equal-priced alternative + the graveyard consequence; cost = body, blocker, clock), so it is not a restatement. The strategy:deckbuilding.ratios citation is gone; the two that remain are verbatim and in context — 'Value is not a win.' opens threat-density's argument that conversion is where decks differ, which is what a drain clock in a three-finisher deck is being priced against. 'painful' is earned.

I judged the weakness -> adequate move hard and it is a defensible reading of the whole section, not a doctor overriding an inconvenient instrument. deck-audit's own notes make the move for it, twice: 'strategy:deckbuilding.ratios is explicit that templates are counts of functions rather than cards and that the counts should come from the deck's actual failure modes — read every target below as a starting point, not a verdict', and 'Under target, but the oracle text shows the function on card(s) the taxonomy did not classify that way — CHECK THESE BEFORE CALLING THE AXIS A WEAKNESS: card-advantage — Kenrith, Kutzil, Loran, Teferi'. The doctor engaged that probe list by name and by oracle text. Both new quotes are verbatim substrings of the fetched section and are the section's own closing argument, not a fragment: 'they are counts of *functions*, not cards' and 'Take the categories, derive the counts from the deck's actual failure modes.' I then counted the functions myself rather than trusting either side: sweeping all 99 oracle texts for draw/into-your-hand gives 13 hits, minus Jegantha (companion boilerplate) and minus Sheoldred (draws nothing) = 11 real card-advantage functions — and the eleventh is Dihada, Binder of Wills's '-3: ... Put any number of legendary cards from among them into your hand', which the taxonomy files protection:self/ramp:treasure and which the audit's probe list does not even name. So 'around eleven, at the template's floor' is grounded from below, not inflated. The corrected 'Real draw, no engine' line is right: Reki 'Whenever you cast a legendary spell, draw a card', Rhystic Study and Esper Sentinel off opponents' spells are all repeatable. Residual I checked and am not opening: Rona's legendary-cast trigger is an UNTAP and her draw is a separate '{T}: Draw a card, then discard a card' — a loot, not net advantage — so 'Rona draws off legendary casts' compresses two abilities into one and slightly overstates that member; it does not move the 10-11 band or the verdict.

The self-directed sweep found the right thing and fixed it correctly. The Dauthi tiebreak no longer prices card advantage; it prices fetchability, and that argument holds against the cards: Dauthi Voidwalker's type line is 'Creature — Dauthi Rogue' (nonlegendary, so Sisay's 'Search your library for a legendary permanent card' can neither fetch nor re-buy it) while Sheoldred is 'Legendary Creature — Phyrexian Praetor' at mana value 4, reachable at power 5. The 'no axis credits it' claim is now symmetric and both halves verify: card_roles files Dauthi threat:body/utility:activated (no interaction or hate role) and Sheoldred draw:engine over an oracle that draws nothing. The quorum premise re-derives: black has 7 pip-bearing cards, ceil(7 x 0.20) = 2, and exactly two costs carry double black. cost_of_cutting still argues AGAINST the cut with 'cut duplicated function before any uncovered class' and 'cover the classes ... before doubling any' — both verbatim, both used in the direction that makes the entry painful rather than easy, which is the honest use of them.

The premise is true and I checked it directly rather than taking it: deck-audit's axes[15] tutors carries target.low = null, target.high = null and verdict 'informational', so the axis has no target and a 2 -> 1 movement genuinely scores nothing. Downgrading it to bookkeeping is right, and the entry does not use the downgrade to empty the cost — what remains is the load-bearing part and it still holds from last round: Kodama is the only net-positive and only repeatable land search in the 99 (the nine fetchlands consume themselves, Path to Exile's basic goes to the opponent), and it is a mana-value-3 green legend, one of the thirteen rungs Sisay reaches at power 4. 'what it loses is a basic-land search, not a card selector' matches the oracle ('search your library for a basic land card'). 'contested' is the right label.

Checked all seven counted cards plus both probes against oracle text, one by one. Six cover Sisay: Boros Charm 'Permanents you control gain indestructible', Flawless Maneuver 'Creatures you control gain indestructible', Heroic Intervention 'hexproof and indestructible', Shalai 'other creatures you control have hexproof' (Sisay is another creature), Flowering of the White Tree 'Legendary creatures you control get +2/+1 and have ward {1}', and Dihada's '+2: Up to one target legendary creature gains vigilance, lifelink, and indestructible'. The seventh, Heliod, Sun-Crowned, is 'Indestructible' as a static on itself and its only activated ability grants lifelink — 'shields nothing else' is exact. Plaza of Heroes reads '{3}, {T}, Exile this land: Target legendary creature gains hexproof and indestructible until end of turn', so 'exiles itself' is literal, and deck-audit's possible_uncounted for this axis is exactly [Katilda, Plaza of Heroes] — the miss is acknowledged from the instrument's own list. The 11 / 88.4% is goldfish_targets' 'Commander protection available' group and goldfish_metrics' assembled_rate 0.884 at mean_turn 2.3; it is labelled 'the engine's protection group', a different set from the counted seven, and engine.components[3] discloses that nine of the eleven are instants. Calling 7 a strength at the top of a 5-7 band is a judgment the reading states plainly ('Seven, the top of the band').

True, and understated in the deck's own favour rather than the doctor's. card_roles.json files Sheoldred, the Apocalypse as ['draw:engine', 'threat:body'] and her oracle contains no draw effect — she is a payoff for drawing, so the role is wrong in the way the gap says. 'missing four that do' is the audit's probe list; my own sweep of the 99 found a fifth uncounted drawer the probe does not name (Dihada's -3 puts legendary cards into your hand), so the floor is one deeper than the gap claims. Filed as a fleet-level instrument defect with a concrete settlement, not used to excuse anything.

Re-ran deck-audit fresh to a slug-scoped path and compared every figure, not just the ones validate-diagnosis re-derives. All 16 measured.value match (40 / 55 / 0 / -15 / 17 / 7 / 8 / 1 / 7 / 3 / 39 / 3 / 0.935 / 3 / 4 / 2), and every reading is consistent with its own value — no 'thin at five beside eleven'. Component sizes 6 / 4 / 7 / 11 match goldfish_targets' four any_of groups exactly, and every rate matches goldfish_metrics: 0.679 mean 4.219, 0.525 (opener 0.258 -> 'four cards, 26% in an opener'), 0.747 mean 2.836, 0.884 mean 2.3. Applied the single-point test in both directions. single_points_of_failure[1] (Najeela) is a REAL single point rather than the 'four independent kills' false positive: all four two_card_infinites in bracket_report.json contain Najeela, so the deck has one kill card with four partners, not four kills. single_points_of_failure[0] names a COST rather than a card, which stretches the schema, but its figures are exact (median cast turn 3, cast_by_turn_6 0.991, mean available mana 4.894 on t5 / 5.869 on t6) and it is the document's central honest finding. components[4] correctly reports the payoff group as undeclared and thinnest — goldfish_targets declares no win line, so the simulation has never measured how this deck kills, which is a defect in the declaration and is named as one.

Ran the orphan check myself rather than relying on the validator: no proposed cut appears in a checker-passed stack's scenario. Sheoldred appears in stacks/001, but 001's checker verdict is fail; 002 (the passing Najeela + Derevi loop) contains none of the five cut cards, and 003 fails. All four adds are Commander-legal and inside the {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} identity (Cryptolith Rite {1}{G} / G, Bear Umbra {2}{G}{G} / G, Beast Within / G, Intruder Alarm {2}{U} / U), and none is prescribed off an obsolescence-index read. Two structural checks pass. First, unverified lines stay unverified: every combo_lines_opened entry is marked 'needs a stack scenario', and the only line asserted as fact anywhere is the Najeela + Derevi loop, which has stacks/002 with checker.verdict == pass and whose caveats the document carries verbatim rather than dropping. Second, add_candidates[3]'s mechanic is stated correctly — Intruder Alarm's untap is applied to dorks already on the battlefield with the ENTERING creature as the trigger, not to the summoning-sick fetch, and its real cost (nine ramp:dork cards stop untapping) is priced. 29 of 33 legendary nonland permanents carry Creature in the type line, as claimed.

The binding conclusion is unchanged and I re-confirm it: no axis binds, the joint {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} bill is the constraint, and gaps[0] records that nothing in the repo measures the joint five-pip event (mana_analysis is per-colour and independent, goldfish reports a scalar). Every premise re-derives against artifacts I fetched today. All 45 citations across axes, cuts, adds, lean_into and the SPOF block are verbatim, whitespace-normalised substrings of the sections they name — checked programmatically against lookup-strategy, zero failures — and the three I judged for context (ratios, threat-density, cutting) are used in the direction their sections argue. The document withholds nothing it can measure and claims nothing it cannot.
